GRANT AGREEMENT

Grant Number: WFF-2026-0417
Date of Agreement: February 11, 2026

Grantee: Riverbend Community Housing Trust, Inc.
Address: 87 Delancey Street, Meridian Falls, Ohio 44708
Employer Identification Number: 34-2871905
Tax Status: Organization described in Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code and classified as a public charity under Section 509(a)(1)

Grant Amount: Seventy-Five Thousand and 00/100 Dollars ($75,000.00) in United States Dollars
Purpose: General operating support
Grant Period: March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027

This Grant Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into between the Whitfield Family Foundation, an Ohio nonprofit corporation (the "Foundation"), and Riverbend Community Housing Trust, Inc. (the "Grantee"). The Foundation is pleased to award the grant described above subject to the terms and conditions set forth below. Please countersign and return one copy of this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date first written above. No funds will be disbursed until the countersigned Agreement is received by the Foundation.

ARTICLE I. PURPOSE AND USE OF FUNDS

1.1 Purpose. The Foundation awards this grant as general operating support for the Grantee's charitable programs serving low- and moderate-income households in Ludlow County, Ohio. General operating support means that the Grantee may apply the funds to any reasonable and necessary expense of carrying out its charitable mission, including personnel, occupancy, technology, professional services, and administrative overhead.

1.2 Charitable Use. The Grantee shall use the grant funds exclusively for charitable, educational, or other exempt purposes within the meaning of Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code. No portion of the grant may be used to carry on propaganda, or otherwise to attempt to influence legislation, within the meaning of Section 4945(d)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code, or to influence the outcome of any specific public election or to carry on, directly or indirectly, any voter registration drive.

1.3 No Regranting. The Grantee shall not regrant, subgrant, or otherwise transfer any portion of the grant funds to another organization or individual without the prior written consent of the Foundation.

ARTICLE II. PAYMENT

2.1 Disbursement. Subject to receipt of the countersigned Agreement, the Foundation will disburse the full grant amount of $75,000.00 in a single payment on or about March 15, 2026, by electronic funds transfer to the account designated by the Grantee in writing.

2.2 Segregation of Records. The Grantee shall account for the grant funds separately within its general ledger so that receipts and expenditures attributable to this grant can be readily identified.

2.3 Unexpended Funds. Any unexpended funds remaining at the conclusion of the Grant Period shall be returned to the Foundation within sixty (60) days after the close of the Grant Period unless the Foundation has approved a written request to retain and apply such funds to the Grantee's continuing operations. Requests to retain unexpended funds must be submitted before February 28, 2027.

ARTICLE III. REPORTING

3.1 Annual Report. The Grantee shall submit a single annual report to the Foundation no later than April 30, 2027. The annual report shall consist of two parts, both submitted together through the Foundation's online grants portal:

     (a) An annual narrative report of not more than eight (8) pages describing the Grantee's activities during the Grant Period, the populations served, significant accomplishments, challenges encountered, and any material changes in strategy or leadership; and

     (b) An annual financial report presenting the Grantee's actual revenue and expenses for the fiscal year in which the Grant Period fell, together with a statement of how the grant funds were applied.

3.2 Form of Report. The Foundation does not prescribe a report template. Reports prepared for the Grantee's board of directors may be submitted if they address the matters listed in Section 3.1.

3.3 Audited Financial Statements. If the Grantee obtains audited financial statements for the fiscal year covered by the Grant Period, a copy shall be provided with the annual report. The Grantee is not required to obtain an audit solely because of this grant.

3.4 Effect of Nonreporting. The Foundation will not consider any future request for support from the Grantee until all reporting required by this Agreement has been received and accepted.

ARTICLE IV. NOTIFICATIONS

4.1 Change in Executive Leadership. The Grantee shall notify the Foundation in writing within thirty (30) days of any change in executive leadership, including the departure, resignation, or replacement of the Executive Director or the Board Chair.

4.2 Change in Tax Status. The Grantee shall notify the Foundation immediately, and in no event later than ten (10) business days, of any change in its tax-exempt status, any notice of examination by the Internal Revenue Service, or any lapse in its registration to solicit charitable contributions in the State of Ohio.

4.3 Material Adverse Events. The Grantee shall promptly notify the Foundation of any litigation, governmental investigation, loss of a major funding source exceeding fifteen percent (15%) of its annual budget, or other event that would materially impair the Grantee's ability to carry out its charitable mission.

ARTICLE V. RECORDS AND ACCESS

5.1 Records Retention. The Grantee shall retain all records relating to the receipt and expenditure of the grant funds for a period of not less than four (4) years following submission of the annual report required by Section 3.1.

5.2 Access. Upon reasonable advance notice, the Foundation or its designated representatives may examine the Grantee's books and records relating to the grant and may visit the Grantee's premises and programs during ordinary business hours.

ARTICLE VI. PUBLICITY AND ACKNOWLEDGMENT

6.1 Acknowledgment. In its annual report, on its website, and in any donor listing published during or after the Grant Period, the Grantee shall acknowledge the Whitfield Family Foundation as a supporter of its general operations. The Grantee shall use the exact name "Whitfield Family Foundation" and shall not use the Foundation's logo without prior written permission.

6.2 Press. The Grantee shall provide the Foundation with a courtesy copy of any press release naming the Foundation at least three (3) business days before its release. The Foundation does not require approval rights over the content of such releases.

ARTICLE VII. GENERAL PROVISIONS

7.1 Independent Contractor. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, employment, or agency relationship between the parties. The Grantee retains complete control over its programs, personnel, and operations.

7.2 Modification. This Agreement may be modified only by a written instrument signed by both parties. Requests for modification should be addressed to the Program Officer identified in Section 7.5.

7.3 Termination and Repayment. The Foundation may suspend or terminate this grant, and may require repayment of all or any part of the grant funds, if the Grantee uses funds for purposes other than those described in Article I, materially breaches this Agreement, ceases to qualify as an organization described in Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, or dissolves. Repayment, if required, shall be made within ninety (90) days of written demand.

7.4 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

7.5 Notices. All notices, reports, and correspondence under this Agreement shall be directed to Elaine Ostrowski, Senior Program Officer, Whitfield Family Foundation, 1220 Corliss Avenue, Suite 400, Meridian Falls, Ohio 44712, or by electronic mail to eostrowski@whitfieldfamilyfound.org.

ARTICLE VIII. ACCEPTANCE

By signing below, the Grantee accepts this grant and agrees to the terms and conditions of this Agreement. The undersigned represents that he or she is authorized to bind the Grantee and that the Grantee remains an organization described in Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code and is not a private foundation within the meaning of Section 509(a).
